summary: The root قثأ (qthA) primarily refers to the cucumber plant and its fruit. It denotes something that grows quickly and is often associated with a specific type of gourd or melon.

provenance.lane: Edward William Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon (1863-93), public domain. Digital text via Perseus, Tufts University, CC BY-SA 3.0 US.
provenance.summary: Editorial summary derived from the Lane entry. NOT Lane's own wording. Shown as a gloss only; the Lane text below is the source.

headwords.def: اقثأت الأَرْضُ, (AZ, S, O,) or اقثأ المَكَانُ, (K,) The land, or the place, abounded with the [ species of cucumber called ] قِثّآء. (AZ, S, O, K.) And اقثأ القَوْمُ The people had abundance of قثّآء. (S, O, K.)

قِثَّآءٌ (S, O, Msb, K) and قُثَّآءٌ, (O, Msb, K,) the former of which, with kesr, in the more common, (Msb, TA,) [ A certain vegetable, ] well-known: (K, TA:) [ a species of cucumber; cucumis sativus β fructu flavo majore: (Delile's Floræ Ægypt. Illustr., no. 928:]) or the [ cucumber called ] خِيَار [q. v.]: (S, O, K:) or a general name for the خِيَار, the عَجُور [q. v.], and the فَقُّوس [or فَقُّوص q.
مَقْثَأَةٌ and مَقْثُؤَةٌ, (S, O, K, TA,) or أَرْضٌ مَقْثَأَةٌ and مَقْثُؤَةٌ, (Msb,) A place, or land, of قثّآء, (S, Msb, K,) where قثّآء are sown and grow. (TA.)

headword_note: Lane indexes geminate roots with two letters where the Corpus uses three; both spellings are resolved here.
